message_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that WBS (a think/don't-think-about-a-named-concept direction from WSB's directed_modulation items) achieves 0.83 on this exact setup. WBS tells the model *what* to think about. This method instead asks the model to *figure out what's implied* without naming anything — an inference stance, not a concept-holding stance.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance direction, built from WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation items (which name a specific concept to hold in mind), lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83. Their contrast tells the model *what* to think about. The open question is whether the inference stance itself — asking the model to figure out *what is implied* without naming it — also carries.
rationale: Both documents explicitly credit Raman et al. (2026) as the source, describe it as a think/don't-think concept-holding stance direction built from directed_modulation items reaching 0.83, and frame the submitted method's novelty identically: an inference stance that figures out what is implied without naming a concept, contrasted with Raman's concept-naming direction. Both also note the same dose-response peak mirroring the source's narrow useful-dose window, so neither document says more or less about the source, the overlap, or the novelty claim than the other.
